name: ELO Digital Office
description: ELO ECM: search the archive by full text or by keywording, walk the folder tree, read a folder's or document's metadata and its change history. Uses the REST interface built into the ELO Indexserver, with Basic auth against your own ELO server. Read-only.
instructions:
**What this connects to.** The ELO Indexserver (IX) publishes its API as REST under `https://<server>/ix-<repository>/rest`: every IX function is a `POST` to `/IXServicePortIF/<function>` with the parameters as a JSON object. This connector uses that interface, so nothing extra has to be installed on a current ELO server (ELO 20 or later). If `https://<server>/ix-<repository>/rest/openapi.json` opens in a browser, the interface is there.

**Setup**
1. Create an ELO user for the integration with read rights on the archive areas the agent should see. ELO applies its access rights to every entry, so a restricted user simply finds less.
2. Set `ELO_URL` to the Indexserver address including the repository, without `/rest` and without a trailing slash, e.g. `https://elo.example.com/ix-Archive`. A server with several repositories needs one connector per repository.
3. Set `ELO_USERNAME` and `ELO_PASSWORD`. They are sent as HTTP Basic auth, which the Indexserver accepts for service clients: it checks them on the first call and reuses the connection, so there is no separate login. Use HTTPS.
4. Start with `elo_get_server_info`: it proves the address and the credentials.

**Everything is a Sord.** ELO stores folders and documents as the same kind of entry, a *Sord*, identified by a numeric object id or a GUID in braces. The `type` field tells them apart: 254 and above are documents, lower values are folders. The root folder has the id `1`.

**Searching is stateful.** `elo_search_fulltext`, `elo_find_by_keywording` and `elo_list_children` return the first page of hits, a `searchId` and `moreResults`. Page with `elo_find_next` (pass `idx`, the position of the first hit to return), and call `elo_find_close` with the `searchId` when you are done, otherwise the Indexserver keeps the result set open. Hits carry their name, date, access list and keywording fields (`objKeys`).

**Full-text search needs ELO iSearch**, the search service that ships with current ELO versions. Without it, use `elo_find_by_keywording` (name, description, keywording form, dates), which reads the database.

**Errors arrive inside a 200 response** as `{"exception": "[ELOIX:...] ..."}`; the connector reports them as errors with ELO's text.

**Self-hosted, which is the thing to plan for.**
- On **AnythingMCP Cloud** the Indexserver must be reachable from the public internet on a real hostname with a valid TLS certificate. A self-signed certificate will fail: the connector offers no trust-anything switch.
- On an internal host (`elo.intern`, `10.0.0.x`), self-host AnythingMCP on the same network and add that host to `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, or the outbound guard refuses the call before it is made.

**Read-only by design**: no tool files, changes, locks or deletes an entry.

ELO_URL.label: Indexserver address
ELO_URL.help: The ELO Indexserver address including the repository, without /rest and without a trailing slash. Your ELO administrator knows it; the web client usually runs on the same host.
ELO_URL.patternMessage: The address must end with the repository part, e.g. https://elo.example.com/ix-Archive, with nothing after it.

tools.name: elo_get_server_info
tools.description: Read the Indexserver's version, instance name and licence information. The quickest proof that the address and the credentials work.

tools.name: elo_search_fulltext
tools.description: Search the repository with ELO iSearch: words in titles, document text and keywording fields. Returns the first page of hits, a searchId and moreResults. Needs iSearch on the ELO server.

query.description: Search terms, e.g. a supplier name or an invoice number.

searchIn.description: Where to look, a comma-separated list of TITLE, FULLTEXT, INDEX_FIELDS, EXTRA_TEXT, FEED, e.g. TITLE,FULLTEXT,INDEX_FIELDS.

tools.name: elo_find_by_keywording
tools.description: Find folders and documents by name, description, keywording form or date, from the database. Combine the fields you know; returns the first page of hits, a searchId and moreResults.

name.description: Words that must appear in the entry's name (case-insensitive).

desc.description: Words that must appear in the entry's description.

maskId.description: Keywording form (mask) id or name, e.g. Invoice.

xDateIso.description: Document date in ELO's ISO form, e.g. 20260131.

iDateIso.description: Filing date in ELO's ISO form, e.g. 20260131.

tools.name: elo_list_children
tools.description: List the entries inside a folder: how to walk the archive from the root (id 1) or a known folder downwards. Returns the first page, a searchId and moreResults.

parentId.description: Object id or GUID of the folder, e.g. 1 for the root.

endLevel.description: How many levels down: 1 for the direct children (default), -1 for all levels.

tools.name: elo_find_next
tools.description: Fetch the next page of an open search with the searchId a search returned. Stop when moreResults is false, then call elo_find_close.

idx.description: Position of the first hit to return, e.g. 50 for the second page of 50.

tools.name: elo_find_close
tools.description: Release an open search on the Indexserver once you have the hits you need.

tools.name: elo_get_sord
tools.description: Read one folder or document by object id or GUID: name, type, dates, owner and parent. Nothing is locked.

objId.description: Object id or GUID of the entry, as returned by a search.

tools.name: elo_get_sord_history
tools.description: Read the change history of one entry: who changed what and when. The audit answer.

objId.description: Object id or GUID of the entry.
